description: A single-panel scanning electron micrograph (captioned as panel "(b)" of Fig. 14) with the instrument annotation "20KV  X10,000" and a "1µm" scale bar printed along the bottom edge. The field of view is grey-scale only — no colour map, no axes, no numeric data labels. Two microstructural components are visible: (i) pale, elongated branch- or dendrite-like arms that run sub-vertically, tapering and splitting as they rise towards the top of the frame, bordered by dark, line-shaped pits (etch grooves or interfacial voids); and (ii) the surrounding matrix, which shows a very fine, periodic, cross-hatched modulation of alternating light and dark striations — the spinodal decomposed structure. The branch arms intrude into and traverse the modulated matrix, which is the point of the figure. The caption identifies the pale branches as δ-ferrite branches within spinodal decomposed γ grains in 12Al-20Mn-1C tempered at 800 °C. The citing text adds that these mixed grains contain δ-ferrite branches linked to δ + κ-carbide lamellar grains extending inside spinodal decomposed γ grains. No magnified inset, diffraction pattern, spectrum or composition map accompanies the micrograph.

observations.observation: The micrograph carries printed instrument annotations '20KV', 'X10,000' and a '1µm' scale bar at the bottom left.
Pale, elongated branch/dendrite-like arms run roughly vertically through the field, tapering and splitting towards the top of the image.
Dark, line-shaped pits or grooves outline and partly replace the boundaries of the pale branches.
The matrix between the branches shows a fine, periodic, cross-hatched pattern of alternating light and dark striations (modulated/spinodal-decomposed microstructure).
The pale branch arms extend into and traverse the finely modulated matrix, i.e. two distinct morphologies coexist within the same field.
The caption states that the image shows δ-ferrite branches within spinodal decomposed γ grains in 12Al-20Mn-1C at 800 °C.

The citing text states that in 12Al-20Mn-1C tempered at 800 °C (Fig. 5(e)) some grains feature a mixed structure in which δ-ferrite branches, linked to δ + κ-carbide lamellar grains, extend inside spinodal decomposed γ grains.
The citing text states that the phenomenon of δ-ferrite branches inside spinodal decomposed γ grains requires further study to be properly understood.

The citing text contrasts this mixed structure with 9Al-10Mn-1C and 12Al-20Mn-1C grades, where cellular-transformed fractions were predominant over spinodal decomposed ones, whereas at 12Al-30Mn-1C only spinodal decomposition involved the entire austenitic volume.
The image alone does not identify the phases; the δ-ferrite / spinodal-decomposed γ assignment comes from the caption, and the κ-carbide lamellar association comes from the citing text.

subfigures.description: Secondary-electron SEM micrograph, 20 kV, ×10,000, 1 µm scale bar. Pale tapering branch-like arms run sub-vertically from the lower edge upward, flanked by dark line-shaped grooves/pits; the intervening matrix exhibits a fine periodic cross-hatched light/dark modulation characteristic of spinodal decomposition. The arms clearly penetrate the modulated matrix.

unreadable_items: No numeric spinodal wavelength/modulation period can be read from the image; the striation spacing is not annotated
The precise crystallographic/phase identity of the pale branches and of the fine striations cannot be determined from the micrograph alone (no EDS/EBSD/SAED inset supplied)
Right and top edges of the micrograph appear slightly cropped, but no informative annotation is lost
